old: Two blocks make a Particle Accelerator easier to run.

The &aAccelerator Magnetic Field&r helps particles through tight turns. Place it inside the ring, then link it with an &2Advanced Target Designator&r saved on the accelerator. Only one field per accelerator counts.

The &aParticle Accelerator Speed Sensor&r gives a redstone signal once particles pass a speed you set, and links the same way. Accelerator Motors also take Speed and Efficiency addons placed underneath them.
new: Two blocks make a Particle Accelerator easier to run.

The &aAccelerator Magnetic Field&r helps particles through tight turns. Place it inside the ring, then link it with an &2Advanced Target Designator&r saved on the accelerator. Only one field per accelerator counts.

The &aParticle Accelerator Speed Sensor&r gives a redstone signal once particles pass a speed you set, and links the same way. Accelerator Motors also take Speed and Efficiency addons placed underneath them.

&eNote&r: In this version the Magnetic Field does not help particles through turns, and the Speed Sensor gives no signal. This is a bug in the mod, so hold off on building them until an update fixes it.
Matter has to come from somewhere.
Build a &aDisintegrator&r. It breaks any item with a matter value into matter, and the pipes carry that matter to your &2Matter Tanks&r.
An item's tooltip shows its matter values. Plentiful items such as cobblestone, dirt and logs are the easiest way to fill your tanks.
Replication machines do nothing on their own. They share power and matter through one network.
Craft &aMatter Network Pipes&r and run them between your machines. Pipes carry power the same way a power cable does, so connect a generator or cable to any pipe and the network gets power.
Each machine has to touch a pipe to join the network.
A &2Disintegrator&r only holds a small amount of matter itself.
Craft a &aMatter Tank&r and connect it to the network. Each tank holds 256,000 of one matter type, and Replicators draw from every tank on the network.
&eNote&r: There are eight matter types, so a busy network will need several tanks. A tank can be locked to one type, given a priority, or set to void its excess.
A pattern on a chip in your inventory is no use to the network.
Craft a &aChip Storage&r and connect it to the network, then put your &2Memory Chip&r in it. It holds 8 chips, and each chip holds 16 patterns.
This pack limits Replication to basic materials and the things crafted or smelted from them.
That covers vanilla ingots, gems, quartz, prismarine, redstone, stone, wood, crops and mob drops, plus silicon, plastics and breeze rods.
A Replicator can run in Infinite Mode, which you turn on from the Replicator's own screen.
In Infinite Mode it keeps making the same item until it is full or the matter runs out, which suits bulk items you always need more of.
The MatterOpedia lists every item's matter values, and you can search it. Open it with the button left of the Replication Terminal's search bar.
Search for a type by name, or filter by amount with earth>10, nether=20 or quantum<6.
An exclamation mark before a type hides items that carry it, and an asterisk shows items that carry only that type (!earth, *metallic).
A Replicator can be pushed a little harder.
Craft a &aReplicator Enclosure&r and Sneak + Right-click a Replicator with it. The Replicator works 20% faster and uses 10% more power.
With matter in the tanks and patterns in storage, the network can build things.
Build a &aReplicator&r and connect it to the network. It builds items from the matter in your tanks, and in this pack it uses 240 FE/t while it works.
The network can only copy an item it has a pattern for.

Build an &aIdentification Chamber&r. It scans an item and writes the pattern to a &2Memory Chip&r. Slow Mode only uses up the item when the scan reaches 100%, while Fast Mode is much quicker but can use up an item on each pass.
&eNote&r: Place a &2Chip Storage&r directly on top of the chamber and new patterns go straight into it, with no chip needed in the chamber.
&2Raw Replica&r smelts into the metal every Replication machine is made from.
Smelt &aReplica Ingots&r in a furnace or blast furnace. Every machine, pipe and chip in this chapter uses them, and the Disintegrator alone takes 13 counting the two &2Matter Tanks&r in its recipe.
Every item breaks down into a mix of eight matter types: Earth, Organic, Metallic, Precious, Living, Nether, Ender and Quantum.
A Replicator uses every type in an item's value, so keep tanks of each type the items you copy need.
Search the MatterOpedia in the Replication Terminal for a type to find cheap items that carry it.
Everything is connected. Now ask the network for something.
Build a &aReplication Terminal&r and connect it to the network. Pick a pattern, set an amount and press Replicate, and the Replicators build the item and send it back to the terminal.
Try it on something cheap first, such as cobblestone, to check that the tanks, pipes and power all work.
One Replication upgrade cannot be crafted directly.
Craft a &aMatter Blueprint&r, which holds the pattern for the &2Replicator Motor&r. Sneak + Right-click a Chip Storage with it to add that pattern to the network.
With the motor's pattern stored, the network can build one.
Replicate a &aReplicator Motor&r from the Terminal, then Sneak + Right-click a Replicator with it. It adds a speed setting, where 100% is normal speed and 20% is the fastest.
&eNote&r: The faster it runs, the higher the chance a print fails. A failed print runs again without using more matter.
&eReplication&r ptinyd items out of raw matter. Break cheap items down, scan the ones you want, and the network can print copies on request.
Everything here is made from one ore that only generates in the &6Mining Dimension&r. Finish the &bMining Dimension&r quest in &6Generating Resources&r and build a &aMining Portal&r before you start.
&eNote&r: In this pack Replication only copies basic materials. Read the What Can Be Copied quest before you plan around an item.
Replica Ore does not generate in the Overworld or any other dimension. It only forms naturally in the deepslate layer of the &6Mining Dimension&r.
Mine &aRaw Replica&r from &2Deepslate Replica Ore&r with an iron pickaxe or better. Veins get more common the deeper you dig, and the most are around Y -63.
A first network takes around 45 ingots, so bring back more than you think you need.
&eNote&r: Later on, Replica also comes from Occultism miners of Afrit tier and above, NauTec's &2Replicophiles&r bacteria and the Asteroid planet of the Interdimensional Laser.
&bCoven Witches&r are the witches who join your coven. Each one you recruit with a signed &aCoven Contract&r counts toward the bigger rites.
A coven rite counts the coven witches within 16 blocks of the &6Golden Ritual Chalk&r. If you carry a &aSeer Stone&r, any recruited witches who are missing are called to the circle.
{@pagebreak}
Coven huts are rare, so the &bSummon Coven Witch&r rite makes one instead. It needs an ordinary witch as a sacrifice, and &bSummon Witch&r ritual can easily bring a witch to you.
&cUse a blank contract.&r The rite eats the one you put in, and losing the signed one disbands your coven.

method_notes: Read-only comparison of old 1.3.2 instance with new 1.4.0 instance. New instance was not modified.
Completed ordinary batches 001-018 only. Batch 019 is incomplete and excluded.
Mod counts are enabled top-level .jar files grouped by declared mod IDs. EuphoriaPatcher was disabled in the old instance, enabled in the new instance.
Ordinary batch counts compare selected English snapshot keys with same resource path in new JARs. Source absence does not prove item removal.
All-native delta compares English and namespace owner together. One ownership-only change is not an English text change.
New-key coverage checks new native Chinese plus the old CFPA archive as a reusable candidate, not an installed or current CFPA layer in the new instance. CJK presence is not semantic verification.
Custom English comparison excludes the ftb_custom namespace authored locally. The 34 custom keys must be migrated, not treated as upstream removals.
Quest structural changes are separate from language changes. Do not replace updated quest structures with old files.
Static source comparison only. No in-game activation, rendering or interaction verification.
cfpa_policy: Direct official GitHub download and integration; no updater mod dependency.
